newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Electricity shares up on bid hopes.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Electricity shares up on bid hopes.

text.p: Shares in Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc were higher in early afternoon trade on Monday as they benefited from speculation that Yorkshire would be the next UK regional electricity company (REC) to succumb to a takeover bid.
Yorkshire shares were 15 pence higher at 792. Greig Middleton analyst David Campbell said the stock could rise as high as 900 pence per share if a bid emerged for the company.
Yorkshire and the larger Southern Electric Plc are the only remaining independent RECs which are not subject to takeover bids. Shares in Southern were unchanged at 775 pence.

Yorkshire is seen as the most attractive of the two becasue of its lower market capitalisation. Analysts said Southern has vowed to retain its independence and would be capable of mounting a strong defence against a takeover.

Greig Middleton's Campbell said the brokerage had advised clients to switch out of London Electricity Plc, which has agreed a 1.267 billion stg takeover by Entergy Corp of the U.S, and into Yorkshire.

Shares in London Electricity were down 15 pence at 681 pence in early afternoon trade as the stock moved ex-dividend. But it is still standing below Entergy's offer price of 705p per share. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
